subject: Outbound controls and allowlist model for Aurora private deployment
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@aurorahealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: infra-team@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-27T15:12:00Z
Subject: Outbound controls for Redwood private deployment - IP allowlisting and egress expectations

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting close to the networking sign-off for the Redwood private deployment into our VPC, but our security team needs clear answers on outbound controls and evidence we can include in the upcoming SOC 2 readiness audit. Two quick asks: 

1) Can you provide the canonical list of IPs/blocks we must allow (control plane, runtime telemetry, storage egress)? We prefer CIDR blocks we can add to our egress firewall rather than per-host DNS allowlists.

2) For tight environments where IP allowlisting isn't acceptable, do you support an alternative proxy/mTLS pattern (customer-managed egress proxy with mTLS to Redwood) or identity-based controls (SNI-only allowlist + cert pinning)? Please call out tradeoffs and any additional operational steps.

I've attached our networking requirements spreadsheet (aurora-requirements.xlsx). We need the info by EOD Friday to feed into procurement and the audit packet. Also helpful: an example runbook or evidence artifact showing Redwood's IP ownership and rotation policy.

Thanks,
Samantha Cho
Security Engineering
Aurora Health

Attachment: aurora-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Outbound controls for Redwood private deployment - IP allowlisting and egress expectations

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. High-level answers up front, then details below: 

- We can provide a stable CIDR allowlist for the Redwood control plane and for object storage endpoints used by private deployments. Those blocks are intended to be small and rotated rarely (rotation windows and notice are described below).
- If your environment cannot allow external CIDRs, the recommended alternative is a customer-managed outbound proxy (forward proxy) with mutual TLS to Redwood control endpoints. We also support an SNI-only allowlist pattern as a lighter-weight (but less robust) option.

Quick tradeoffs: 
* Static CIDR allowlist: simplest for firewall teams; minimal runtime changes; requires accepting our announced rotation window. Best for strict egress policies and SOC evidence because IP ownership is auditable.
* Customer-managed proxy + mTLS: no external CIDRs required; you retain egress control and can centralize egress inspection. Requires configuration for mTLS certs on both sides and a short onboarding window. More operational overhead but best for zero-trust oriented networks.
* SNI-only allowlist: low operational lift (allow TLS to control hostnames); susceptible to co-hosting risks and does not provide per-tenant identity — use only for low-risk telemetry or if other options are blocked.

Proposed deliverables by EOD Friday (I can deliver Monday if you need more time):
1) aurora-egress-ip-list.csv — canonical CIDRs and service mapping (controlplane, telemetry, object-store).
2) redwood-egress-runbook-v1.pdf — short runbook with firewall examples, rotation cadence, and evidence we provide for audits.
3) checklist of proxy + mTLS steps if you choose that route.

Sample firewall snippets we recommend (place these as outbound egress rules from your application subnets):
- allow tcp 443 to controlplane-api.redwood-inference.com (52.32.120.0/29) — purpose: control plane API calls
- allow tcp 443 to obj-storage.redwood-inference.com (3.234.56.78/32, 3.234.56.79/32) — purpose: model/asset fetch + checkpointing
- allow udp/tcp 123 to ntp.redwood-inference.com (13.224.0.0/28) — purpose: time sync for audit logs

Operational notes: 
- Rotation notice: we publish planned rotations at least 7 business days in advance and provide signed attestations of IP allocations for audit use.
- Evidence: we can provide signed allocation statements, ASN/WHOIS references, and a short packet showing our egress NAT topology for the private deployment.

I'll attach the CIDR CSV and runbook in my next message. If you can tell me whether your cluster egress is NATed through a central egress gateway or if each host has its own public IP, that helps us recommend the exact rule set.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@aurorahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Outbound controls for Redwood private deployment - IP allowlisting and egress expectations

Morning all — attaching the CSV with the blocks we expect Aurora to allow. I've tried to keep the blocks as small as operationally feasible. 

Attached: aurora-egress-ip-list.csv (three columns: service, cidr, purpose) and redwood-egress-runbook-v1.pdf. Key details below for your firewall team: 

Authoritative list (example entries):
- controlplane-api.redwood-inference.com -> 52.32.120.0/29 -> Control plane API (TLS 443).
- obj-storage.redwood-inference.com -> 3.234.56.78/32, 3.234.56.79/32 -> Model asset fetch (TLS 443).
- telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.com -> 34.217.8.64/28 -> Metrics & health telemetry (TLS 443).
- registry-downloads.redwood-inference.com -> 54.210.12.128/30 -> Initial model layer pulls (TLS 443).

Firewall rule recommendations (outbound):
1) From: app-subnet-*-prod -> To: 52.32.120.0/29 port 443 (control plane).
2) From: app-subnet-*-prod -> To: 3.234.56.78/32, 3.234.56.79/32 port 443 (object storage).
3) Allow DNS (udp/53) to your resolver; do NOT rely on public DNS name allowlists for control-plane security.
4) If you run an egress proxy, configure mTLS connection to controlplane-api.redwood-inference.com and allow only the proxy's IPs in the firewall.

Audit and evidence notes: 
- We will provide an IP allocation attest (signed PDF) and a tarball of sample egress logs (redacted) showing connection patterns for an identical private deployment used in a previous customer POC.
- Rotation cadence: we aim for quarterly review; emergency rotations will be announced 7 business days in advance where possible.

If Aurora confirms that your egress is NATed to a single egress gateway, please share that gateway IP(s) and we'll boil the list down to a single allowed remote IP. If you NAT at host level, we'll need to keep the CIDR blocks as-is.

Next step: Samantha — can you confirm whether you prefer the static-CIDR approach or the egress-proxy + mTLS approach? We can schedule a 30-minute runbook walk-through this week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: aurora-egress-ip-list.csv, redwood-egress-runbook-v1.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@aurorahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Outbound controls for Redwood private deployment - IP allowlisting and egress expectations

Samantha / Aurora infra team — thanks for the rapid coordination. From Product Ops perspective this plan looks good; a couple of final asks to make this audit-ready:

1) Please accept Redwood's proposed rotation notice of 7 business days for planned IP changes. We will not rotate more frequently than that outside of emergencies.
2) For audit purposes, we'll provide an "IP allocation statement" PDF and a short digest of flow logs covering a 30-day window once you complete first-week production traffic. That should satisfy the SOC 2 evidence requirement on egress ownership.

Operational clarification: we recommend a minimum DNS TTL of 300s if you select any hostname-based rules; lower TTLs increase churn in ephemeral environments. Also: if Aurora uses a central NAT gateway, whitelist that gateway only — it'll simplify your firewall change process.

I'll also drop a Confluence snippet and the DocuSign network statement in the related links for sign-off. Marissa / Rishi — please add the signed allocation PDF to the Confluence page after it's created so Aurora's auditors can fetch it.

Happy to join the runbook call if useful; propose 2027-04-29 10:00 PT.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
